transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: Tue Oct 06 2026 14:00 PDT | Duration: 52 minutes | Recorded: yes
- Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Evan Cho (Redwood SE); Alicia Marquez (Bristlepoint), Samir Patel (Bristlepoint DevOps), Helen Song (Bristlepoint Security), Leo Grant (Bristlepoint Product)

Auto-summary (may be rough):
Redwood runthrough of onboarding flow, talked through VPC options and network chart. Customer emphasized data residency, SAML SSO, and KMS. SE flagged possible firewall egress requirements; decision to test VPC peering and then spin up a Dedicated pilot cluster. Pricing worksheet to follow, plus runbook.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Hayes: okay uh hey everyone thanks for joining on time, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm going to run the kickoff with Priya and Evan. welcome.
[00:08] Alicia Marquez: thanks Jordan, appreciate it. we pulled together the infra and security folks — Samir and Helen are on. goal for today is to make sure we can start the pilot in two weeks and we understand networking and keys.
[00:20] Priya Nair: hi all, quick agenda: introductions, runbook highlights, network and security intake, pilot success criteria, and next steps. should take ~45. wow that math is off — okay 45 to 60 minutes.
[00:33] Evan Cho: i'll cover the infra bits mostly — vpc pairing, kube bits, and example terraform. forgive me if i talk too infra-y.
[00:40] Samir Patel: great, yes we're primarily AWS, us-east-1, we have transit gateway style setup, and our security team wants dedicated capacity behind a private VPC for PII-sensitive requests.
[00:50] Helen Song: we need SOC2 evidence, audit log capture, and KMS integration. also SAML SSO for console access.
[00:58] Jordan Hayes: perfect, that's in line with many of our dedicated/private customers. quick question — is `data residency` a hard requirement or is it more about egress control?
[01:08] Alicia Marquez: mostly egress and encryption at rest, we want keys we own. residency is nice to have but not blocking.
[01:15] Evan Cho: good — so KMS-HSM flow works on our Private offering. for Dedicated we can either bring-your-own-KMS or onboard into Redwood-managed keys with customer KMS wrapping; we'll document options.
[01:27] Leo Grant: can you explain the tradeoffs again between Dedicated vs Hosted? we've got cost sensitivity and also latency concerns for user-facing suggestions.
[01:35] Jordan Hayes: sure — hosted is fastest to start and lower operational lift, but less isolation; Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and predictable throughput — higher cost but SLOs; Private/VPC gives full control but longer setup. Evan, maybe you can map latency/cost numbers?
[01:48] Evan Cho: briefly — for our typical suggestion workload, hosted median p95 latency is 80-120ms on our curated models; Dedicated reduces jitter and can cut p95 to 40-70ms depending on batch config. cost delta depends on utilization; we'll send model-profile numbers.
[02:06] Samir Patel: okay useful. for pilot we'd be fine with slightly higher latency if unit cost is low, but production needs p95 < 120 and 99.9 uptime.
[02:16] Jordan Hayes: noted. moving on to network — Evan, walk through the network diagram.
[02:22] Evan Cho: so two options: 1) VPC peering (we do VPC peering or AWS Transit GW peering) so traffic stays inside aws; 2) Private Link for egress-controlled endpoints. For peering we'll need your CIDR ranges, route table updates, and security group rules. we also need to know if outbound egress is restricted to a small set of IPs.
[02:42] Samir Patel: outbound egress is locked down to a few NAT gateways and security team needs a allowlist of IPs. can you give us an egress IP list?
[02:49] Evan Cho: yes we'll provide a short-lived egress IP set for the pilot; for long-term we recommend using PrivateLink or our VPC connector so you don't open wide ranges.
[02:58] Helen Song: can you confirm log collection works with our SIEM? we centralize CloudTrail and also expect audit logs from Redwood console actions.
[03:06] Priya Nair: we ingest and ship audit logs to your S3 or to the SIEM via forwarder — we can do both. Jordan, quick note: we have an audit log retention and export guide i'll attach.
[03:16] Jordan Hayes: i'll drop that after the call. timeline question — Alicia you said two weeks for pilot start?
[03:22] Alicia Marquez: yes, two weeks would be ideal. we have a blackout week next week but the following week should be clear.
[03:28] Jordan Hayes: alright, so target pilot kickoff 2026-10-20 then.
[03:33] Leo Grant: pilot success metrics — we want throughput for automated suggestions at 200QPS sustained, p95 <120ms, and quality metrics (top-click CTR vs baseline).
[03:44] Evan Cho: note on QPS — that'll determine whether Dedicated capacity is required. for 200QPS sustained we usually recommend reserved capacity unless batching is extremely efficient.
[03:55] Samir Patel: what's the onboarding process for service accounts and IAM roles? we'll need least privilege access.
[03:59] Evan Cho: we'll provide a terraform module and example IAM policies; you'll create an IAM role for Redwood service account to assume with a short-lived role for setup. action: Evan will share the terraform link.
[04:12] Jordan Hayes: i'm going to record that as an action.
[04:15] [05:00] Jordan Hayes: (paraphrasing) i also want to call out observability — our console can emit per-route token cost breakdowns and trace hooks. does your team want traces in jaeger or splunk?
[05:12] Helen Song: splunk for now, but we might add jaeger later. export cadence is important.
[05:17] Priya Nair: we can set up log forwarding to splunk, and also create a dashboard template for the pilot. i'll include that in the runbook.
[05:25] Samir Patel: are there any pre-shared artifacts you need from our side?
[05:28] Priya Nair: yes — CIDR ranges, contact for firewall ticket, list of prompt types with sample inputs (for quality monitoring), and SAML metadata for SSO.
[05:39] Alicia Marquez: we'll get that to you by EOD Friday.
[05:43] Jordan Hayes: perfect. quick question on data retention and deletion for logs — Helen mentioned compliance. we have configurable retention and can provide on-demand purging; dev team?
[05:56] Helen Song: as long as we can demonstrate deletion and have an audit trail, that should be fine.
[06:02] Jordan Hayes: noted. switching to pilot plan — scope is: 1) connectivity test, 2) staging ingest and simple inference run, 3) latency and cost profiling, 4) quality check using your prompt sets. timeline two weeks.
[06:18] Leo Grant: for quality checks — can you take our labeled test set and run evals?
[06:22] Evan Cho: yes our Optimize toolkit can run the evals and generate regression alerts; we'll need the set and desired metrics.
[06:29] Samir Patel: any secrets exposure concerns with prompts? we have PII in some examples, so we prefer to mask before sharing.
[06:35] Priya Nair: absolutely — share a masked set or synthetic data. we can still run alignment checks.
[06:40] Jordan Hayes: ok moving into specific permissions — Helen, do you have any blockers with the proposed service account model?
[06:45] Helen Song: the only blocker is KMS key access; we want to bring our own KMS, so we need a walkthrough on key policy and key wrapping.
[06:53] Evan Cho: we support BYOK and bring-your-own-kms policies; the walkthrough is fairly standard — we'll send a short spec.
[06:59] [08:00] Samir Patel: network test plan: what does a connectivity test look like?
[08:05] Evan Cho: simple — we ask you to create a small ec2 instance in the staging VPC and allow ssh; we'll run a curl to our endpoint to validate TLS and route. then we'll test prefix/KV cache behavior with a tiny inference job.
[08:20] Jordan Hayes: that should take under an hour if firewall allows.
[08:24] Alicia Marquez: good. question on scaling: we may burst seasonally; how do autoscaling policies work with Dedicated?
[08:33] Evan Cho: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst pools; you can set policies by CPU/GPU utilization or queue depth. we also have a fallback policy to route traffic to hosted model variants if capacity is low.
[08:45] Leo Grant: fallback sounds useful, any risk of latency spikes?
[08:49] Evan Cho: small spike, but fallback is to a compatible model family with similar output; we'll define thresholds in the rollout policy.
[08:58] Jordan Hayes: moving to administrative stuff — SAML SSO: who manages identity?
[09:03] Helen Song: we use Okta. we'll provide metadata and group mapping; console access only for specific roles.
[09:09] Priya Nair: we have an SSO guide; we'll map Redwood roles to your Okta groups.
[09:14] Samir Patel: anything around PCI/PII flows? some of our customers' data is payment-adjacent.
[09:19] Jordan Hayes: we recommend redaction on the client side; also Private deployment is recommended when you have strict PCI requirements. we'll share the compliance pack.
[09:28] Alicia Marquez: ok. can we get pricing for a one-month Dedicated pilot vs hosted pilot?
[09:33] Jordan Hayes: yes — Jordan to share pricing worksheet and a recommended pilot configuration.
[09:37] Evan Cho: i'll attach model profile perf numbers and a terraform module in the follow-up.
[09:42] [12:00] Leo Grant: question — how do rollouts look? we want canary then full. does Redwood support canary and canary metric gating?
[12:08] Priya Nair: yes rollouts allow canary, A/B, and automatic fallback. gating can be tied to latency or quality regressions against a prompt set.
[12:18] Samir Patel: perfect. for the pilot we'll probably do a small canary at 5% traffic then bump.
[12:24] Jordan Hayes: noted; we'll put that in the runbook.
[12:28] Alicia Marquez: any other blockers from security?
[12:31] Helen Song: just the KMS and audit/demo of deletion. otherwise looks good.
[12:36] Jordan Hayes: great. quick recap: Jordan to send pricing and runbook; Priya will schedule recurring two-week sprint and create dashboard template; Evan will share terraform and VPC test steps; customer will send CIDRs, Okta metadata, masked prompt sets, and open the firewall ticket. target pilot kickoff 2026-10-20.
[12:58] Priya Nair: i'll send the calendar invite with stakeholders and link to the runbook right after this.
[13:05] Samir Patel: we'll start the network ticket today.
[13:09] Jordan Hayes: perfect, thanks everyone. any last comments?
[13:12] Leo Grant: no, thanks. looking forward.
[13:15] Jordan Hayes: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[13:20] [End of recording, rough transcription — some audio dropouts around 00:45 and 08:10, occasional word confusions like "K V cash" for KV cache]
